metadata.title: Team Theory Foundations — Sources
metadata.description: Primary references for 10 team-theory primitives: team decision problem, information structure, person-by-person optimality, value of communication, Radner's LQG theorem, Witsenhausen counterexample, information cost, organizational forms, Dec-POMDP / MARL extension, common-task condition. Marschak–Radner classical layer plus modern multi-agent LLM extensions.

canonical_texts.name: Elements for a Theory of Teams
canonical_texts.description: Marschak (1955). Management Science 1(2):127–137. Founding paper of team theory; defines team decision problem, information structure, common-task condition. Primary source for primitives #1, #2, #10.

canonical_texts.name: Team Decision Problems
canonical_texts.description: Radner (1962). Annals of Mathematical Statistics 33(3):857–881. Proves linear-quadratic-Gaussian team optimality theorem. Primary source for primitive #5 (Radner's LQG theorem) and #3 (person-by-person optimality).

canonical_texts.name: Economic Theory of Teams
canonical_texts.description: Marschak and Radner (1972). Yale University Press. Canonical book-length treatment of team theory. Covers all classical primitives. Primary source for primitives #1, #2, #3, #4, #5, #7.

canonical_texts.name: A Counterexample in Stochastic Optimum Control
canonical_texts.description: Witsenhausen (1968). SIAM Journal on Control 6(1):131–147. Shows nonlinear policies strictly dominate linear in a non-classical two-stage LQG team. Primary source for primitive #6.

canonical_texts.name: Implications of Rational Inattention
canonical_texts.description: Sims (2003). Journal of Monetary Economics 50(3):665–690. Information-cost framework that translates to bounded-rationality team problems. Primary source for primitive #7 (information cost).

canonical_texts.name: The Architecture of Economic Systems: Hierarchies and Polyarchies
canonical_texts.description: Sah and Stiglitz (1986). American Economic Review 76(4):716–727. Compares hierarchical and polyarchical organizational forms under noisy information. Primary source for primitive #8.

canonical_texts.name: The Organization of Decentralized Information Processing
canonical_texts.description: Radner (1993). Econometrica 61(5):1109–1146. Formal model of organizational form selection under information processing constraints. Primary source for primitive #8.

canonical_texts.name: The Complexity of Decentralized Control of Markov Decision Processes
canonical_texts.description: Bernstein, Givan, Immerman, Zilberstein (2002). Mathematics of Operations Research 27(4):819–840. Establishes NEXP-completeness of finite-horizon Dec-POMDP. Primary source for primitive #9.

canonical_texts.name: A Concise Introduction to Decentralized POMDPs
canonical_texts.description: Oliehoek and Amato (2016). Springer. Modern textbook treatment of Dec-POMDPs and MARL. Primary source for primitive #9.

canonical_texts.name: The Surprising Effectiveness of PPO in Cooperative Multi-Agent Games
canonical_texts.description: Yu et al. (2022). NeurIPS. Multi-Agent PPO (MAPPO) with centralized training, decentralized execution. Modern MARL benchmark for cooperative team problems. Secondary source for primitive #9.

canonical_texts.name: QMIX: Monotonic Value Function Factorisation for Deep Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
canonical_texts.description: Rashid et al. (2018). ICML. Value-decomposition method for cooperative MARL. Secondary source for primitive #9.

canonical_texts.name: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?
canonical_texts.description: Cemri et al. (2025). NeurIPS. Empirical taxonomy of 14 multi-agent LLM failure modes across 1,600+ traces, grouped into system design issues, inter-agent misalignment, and task verification. Primary modern source for translating team-theory primitives to LLM agent failures.

canonical_texts.name: Reinforcement Learning for LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems through Orchestration Traces
canonical_texts.description: Decomposes orchestration into five sub-decisions: spawn, delegate, communicate, aggregate, stop. Direct application of team-theoretic structure to LLM agent design. Secondary source for primitives #2, #4, #8. Title and existence re-verified via direct arXiv fetch 2026-08-14 (author: Chenchen Zhang, submitted May 2026).

canonical_texts.name: Coordination as an Architectural Layer for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
canonical_texts.description: Argues coordination should be a configurable layer separate from agent logic. Aligns with team-theoretic separation of information structure from decision rules. Secondary source for primitives #2, #8.

canonical_texts.name: Team Decision Theory and Information Structures
canonical_texts.description: Y.-C. Ho (1980). Proceedings of the IEEE 68(6):644–654. Survey of team decision theory and information structure taxonomy. Secondary source for primitives #2, #3.

canonical_texts.name: Agreeing to Disagree
canonical_texts.description: Aumann (1976). Annals of Statistics 4(6):1236–1239. Common-knowledge result connecting team-theoretic shared belief to formal common ground. Boundary reference between team theory and grounding-communication.

canonical_texts.name: Single-Agent LLMs Outperform Multi-Agent Systems on Multi-Hop Reasoning Under Equal Thinking Token Budgets
canonical_texts.description: Tran & Kiela (2026). arXiv cs.CL. Controlled empirical comparison of single-agent vs. five multi-agent architectures (sequential, subtask-parallel, parallel-roles, debate, ensemble) across Qwen3, DeepSeek-R1, Gemini 2.5 families. Single agents consistently match or exceed multi-agent on multi-hop reasoning under equal token budgets. Grounded in the Data Processing Inequality. Corroborated by Cemri et al. (2025, MAST, NeurIPS, arXiv:2503.13657) and Dochkina (2026, arXiv:2603.28990). Source for primitive #4 (value of communication, negative case) and #7 (information cost). Title and authors (Dat Tran, Douwe Kiela) re-verified via direct arXiv fetch 2026-08-14.

canonical_texts.name: Latent Collaboration in Multi-Agent Systems (LatentMAS)
canonical_texts.description: Zou et al. (2025), Latent Collaboration in Multi-Agent Systems. Primary Section 4.1: reported average accuracy improvements over single-model baseline are 14.6% sequential and 13.3% hierarchical; gains over TextMAS are 2.8% and 4.6%. Average speedups versus sequential/hierarchical TextMAS are 4×/4.3×, output-token reductions 70.8%/83.7%. Nine benchmarks, specialized shared latent-memory architecture; representation compatibility and local comparisons required. Preserve authors units, no unsupported percentage-point conversion. Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.20639#S4.SS1; checked 2026-09-17.

canonical_texts.name: Drop the Hierarchy and Roles: How Self-Organizing LLM Agents Outperform Designed Structures
canonical_texts.description: Dochkina (2026). IEEE Access (submitted). 25,000-task empirical comparison of 8 coordination protocols (rigid hierarchy to emergent self-organization) across 8 LLMs and 4–256 agent configurations. Self-organizing sequential protocol outperforms centralized orchestration by 14% (Cohen's d=1.86, p<0.0001) and scales sub-linearly to 256 agents. Open-source models achieve 95% of closed-source quality at 24× lower cost. Corroborated by CARD (Wu et al., ICLR 2026, arXiv:2603.01089) and MegaAgent (ACL 2025). Source for primitive #8 (fourth organizational form: emergent self-organization) and #3 (role co-optimization beyond PBPO). Title, author (Victoria Dochkina), March 2026 submission, and the 14% improvement figure re-verified via direct arXiv fetch 2026-08-14. Note tension with Pappu2026ExpertsHeldBack: self-organization helps structural coordination but does not fix competence-weighted aggregation.

canonical_texts.name: Understanding the Information Propagation Effects of Communication Topologies in LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
canonical_texts.description: Shen, Liu, Dai et al. (2025). arXiv cs.MA. Causal empirical study showing non-monotonic effect of topology density on LLM multi-agent task performance: moderately sparse topologies optimally suppress error propagation while preserving beneficial information diffusion. Proposes EIB-Learner adaptive topology. Corroborated by CARD (Wu et al., ICLR 2026, arXiv:2603.01089) and AgentsNet (July 2025, arXiv:2507.08616). Source for primitive #2 (topology as information structure design variable) and #4 (non-monotonic value of communication in dense agent graphs).

canonical_texts.name: Human-AI teaming in healthcare: 1 + 1 > 2?
canonical_texts.description: Liu, Zhang, Chen, and Chen (2025). npj Artificial Intelligence (Nature portfolio), December 2025, DOI 10.1038/s44387-025-00052-4. Authors confirmed 2026-07-11. Reliability analysis of 52 empirical clinical studies. Finds that teaming interaction mode (simultaneous vs. sequential) and clinician expertise (juniors benefit more than seniors) are the primary moderators of human-AI team complementarity; simultaneous mode (parallel observation) outperforms sequential mode (cascaded observation). Corroborated by Kargarnovin, Hernandez, Reiners, Cruz-Neira, Bochenek & Karwowski (2026, Frontiers in Robotics and AI, DOI 10.3389/frobt.2026.1733942, PRISMA review of 104 studies) and Gonzalez, Donahue, Goldstein, Heidari, Jalali, Schelble, Singh & Woolley (2026, PNAS Nexus 5(3):pgag030, complementarity framework). Both corroborating papers verified to exist 2026-07-11. Source for primitive #2 (temporal information structure in human-AI teams) and #8 (organizational form: simultaneous vs. sequential observation).

canonical_texts.name: Psychological Safety Comes of Age: Observed Themes in an Established Literature
canonical_texts.description: Edmondson, A.C. and Bransby, D.P. (2023). Annual Review of Organizational Psychology and Organizational Behavior 10:55–78. Field's authoritative state-of-the-literature review. Establishes that psychological safety robustly benefits learning and adaptive performance; cites Eldor, Hodor & Cappelli (2023, see PsychSafetyNonlinear2023) as the primary empirical basis for a curvilinear boundary condition (high psych safety can harm routine in-role performance). Primary source for P0-A Anti-Pattern row. URL is Annual Reviews DOI-stable; full-text access requires subscription — url_check manual. Re-verified 2026-07-11: title/authors/journal/volume/pages confirmed via multiple secondary listings (SciRP, HBS faculty page).

canonical_texts.name: The limits of psychological safety: Nonlinear relationships with performance
canonical_texts.description: Eldor, Hodor, and Cappelli (2023). Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes 177, article 104255. Five independent studies (nursing plus four other organizational settings) show routine in-role task performance rises with psychological safety only to a point, then declines (inverted-U); collective accountability moderates the downside. Primary empirical source for the curvilinear claim; Edmondson & Bransby (2023) cites it as the field's key nonlinearity finding. Article number, authors, journal, and volume re-confirmed 2026-08-14.
canonical_texts.verification_note: Re-verified 2026-08-14: title, authors, volume 177, article 104255 confirmed via multiple secondary listings (TAU CRIS, PsycNet, AHRQ PSNet). Full text still paywalled on ScienceDirect, so effect sizes remain hedged. No independent replication located as of 2026-08-14. A practitioner critique (Geraghty, psychsafety.com, 2023 — blog, not peer-reviewed) raises supervisor-rating bias and questions whether the 80–90th-percentile turning point is a statistical artifact; noted in the skill as a reason to hedge, not cited as evidence.

canonical_texts.name: Team Virtuality and Innovation
canonical_texts.description: Sinnemann & Weiss (2025). Journal of Organizational Behavior 46:867–888. Meta-analysis of 132 independent samples, N=7,004 teams, 167 effect sizes. Finds no significant main effect of team virtuality on team innovation; effect is significantly moderated by task type (divergent tasks: virtuality-tolerant; convergent tasks: virtuality hurts) and communication technology (video > audio > text for innovation). Primary source for P1-A Decision Checklist item and Virtual Team Design pattern. URL returned 402 during verification; high confidence from multiple secondary sources confirming existence and findings.
canonical_texts.verification_note: Primary URL returned 402 (paywall). Existence and findings confirmed at HIGH confidence via audit secondary sources.

canonical_texts.name: Transactive Memory Systems in Organizations: Matching Tasks, Expertise, and People
canonical_texts.description: Brandon, D.P. and Hollingshead, A.B. (2004). Organization Science 15(6):633-644. Establishes TMS as a shared cognitive division of labor: members specialize in different knowledge domains, and the team maintains a shared directory of expertise. Three measurable dimensions: specialization, credibility, coordination. Task structure is a primary developmental influence. Primary source for P0-B TMS analog in Primitive #2. Verified: title, authors (first-author order confirmed — Brandon is first author), year, journal, page range, and core claims confirmed via direct fetch and secondary listings (RePEc/IDEAS) 2026-07-11.

canonical_texts.name: Complementarity in Human-AI Collaboration: Concept, Sources, and Evidence
canonical_texts.description: Hemmer, Schemmer, Kühl, Vössing, Satzger (2024). European Journal of Information Systems (2025). Formalizes complementary team performance (CTP) — human-AI output exceeding either alone. CTP is rare in practice. Two necessary conditions for CTP: (1) information asymmetry (human holds local context AI lacks) and (2) capability asymmetry (human provides judgment on novel cases). Two empirical studies confirm these as viable CTP pathways. Primary source for P1-B CTP conditions in Composition Recipes and Trap in patterns-scenarios-traps.md. Verified via arXiv abstract fetch.

canonical_texts.name: Multi-Agent Teams Hold Experts Back
canonical_texts.description: Pappu et al. (2026), Multi-Agent Teams Hold Experts Back. Primary Table 2 / Section 4.2: HLE Text-Only Expert Not Mentioned team 28.0%, At Least One Correct oracle 47.5%, relative synergy gap 41.1%; best fixed individual 29.0%, Reveal Expert team 36.0%. The 41.1% is an oracle gap, not loss against the best individual, despite broad abstract wording. Psychology experiments separately investigate expertise dilution and team size. Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.01011#S4.SS2; checked 2026-09-17. Supports explicit aggregation comparison, not a universal deference rule.

canonical_texts.name: g versus c: comparing individual and collective intelligence across two meta-analyses
canonical_texts.description: Rowe, Hattie, and Hester (2021). Cognitive Research: Principles and Implications. Meta-analysis pooling 857 groups across nine criterion tasks from eight independent samples. Finds the collective-intelligence c-factor correlates only r=.26 (95% CI .10–.40) with external group performance, and that all but four studies (five independent samples, N=366 groups) failed to control for members' individual intelligence. Primary source for the contested status of the c-factor in primitives-overview #2 and the collective-intelligence Anti-Pattern row. Authors, journal, group count, correlation, and the individual-IQ control caveat verified via PMC full text 2026-08-14.

canonical_texts.name: High-performing teams: Is collective intelligence the answer?
canonical_texts.description: Rowe, Hattie, and Munro (2024). PLOS ONE 19:e0307945. 85 participants in 29 groups. Contrary to Woolley et al.'s (2010) hypothesized single-factor model, findings favor a two-factor cFluid/cCrystal structure grounded in Cattell's fluid/crystallized distinction. Small sample — supports 'contested,' not 'refuted.' Corroborates RoweHattieHester2021. Title, authors, year, journal, sample size, and two-factor finding verified via direct fetch 2026-08-14. Source for the collective-intelligence caveat in primitives-overview #2 and patterns-scenarios-traps.md.

canonical_texts.name: The Mythical Man-Month: Essays on Software Engineering
canonical_texts.description: Brooks, F.P. (1975; 20th-anniversary ed. 1995). Addison-Wesley. Establishes that adding personnel to a late software project makes it later, because pairwise communication paths grow combinatorially (~n(n-1)/2) with team size while individual output does not. Long-standing, uncontested management-of-engineering classic; used here only as the qualitative mechanism (quadratic coordination-link growth), not as a quantitative team-theory result. Primary source for P0-C team-size / coordination-cost curve in primitives-overview.md #8b.

canonical_texts.name: Accelerate: The Science of Lean Software and DevOps — Building and Scaling High Performing Technology Organizations
canonical_texts.description: Forsgren, N., Humble, J., Kim, G. (2018). IT Revolution. Source for references/westrum-culture-measurement.md: Westrum's three-culture typology (Table 3.1, printed p. 65) and the seven validated Likert items measuring team organizational culture (Ch. 13, printed pp. 191-192). Used as the measured-culture empirical counterpart to the Marschak-Radner information-structure primitives, NOT as a source of team-theory results. Provenance limits: self-reported 2016-era survey population; inferential-predictive design, so findings are 'associated with' outcomes except where the authors' own directional prediction is quoted; the book's retired high/medium/low performer tiers are not cited as current fact.

canonical_texts.name: Team Decision Theory and Information Structures in Optimal Control Problems—Part I
canonical_texts.description: Ho & Chu (1972), IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control 17(1), 15–22. Primary partially nested information-structure result; action-dependent observations alone do not establish non-classical structure.
